answer: Each storage provider must answer random Merkle challenges against a sealed sector: the registry picks a leaf by hash and the provider returns the leaf plus its path to the sector root. A delta of doubt triggers a re-audit, and a provider holding only a ember of the data fails the path check. Every challenge binds to the provider key, so one stored copy proves exactly one identity, and a karst of fake replicas collapses under the first random leaf.
